rules: This baseline may only SHRINK. CI rejects any commit that adds an entry.
A new unprotected mutating action fails the build - it is not silently appended.
A protected or removed action must disappear from this file.
Renaming a controller or action does NOT create a new allowance: the id changes, so the old id becomes stale (diagnostic CBA007) and the new id is unlisted (CBA001 error).
No blanket suppression. No project-wide disable switch.

The 'gaps' figure and the entries list are the ENFORCED invariant and may only shrink. The mutating, attributeProtected and inBodyProtected figures are descriptive totals of the tree and legitimately grow when protected endpoints are added; frozenBaselineHistory records every such change with its reason.

frozenBaselineHistory.stage: Central Documents Batch 3 HTTP + Restaurant Batch 3 UI, integration wave (TAB-1, 2026-08-31)
frozenBaselineHistory.note: MEASURED, NOT CARRIED. Two earlier handoffs proposed controller counts for this integration - 49 -> 50 from the Client Portal batch, and a 50 -> 51 already spent by project closeout. Neither was applied: the scanner was run against the real candidate before and after, and it answered 51 -> 52. The Client Portal figure also named CrossBuy.Tests/ReconciliationTests.cs, a file that does not exist; the frozen constants live in CrossBuy.Analyzers.Tests. A count copied from a report is a guess about a tree somebody else was holding. THREE new mutating endpoints, all on the EXISTING DocumentsController, so the endpoint total moves by three while the controller total moves by one for a different reason (below): Documents/submit, Documents/{id}/verify and Documents/{id}/reject. All three carry [ValidateAntiForgeryToken]; submit also carries [RequestSizeLimit] so the cap applies before the body is read. THEY ARE IN-BODY PROTECTED, AND THAT REQUIRED AN ANALYZER CHANGE RATHER THAN A BASELINE ENTRY. They authorize one layer down, in IPlatformDocumentService, which asks IDocumentAccessResolver before it touches a row - the whole design of ADR-040, in which a central document controller is forbidden to know how document permission works. CBA001 could not see that and refused to compile them. The three ways out were a suppression, a baseline entry, or declaring the two types as authorities; the first two record a real gap where there is none, so the third was taken. THE DECLARATION WAS PROVEN BEFORE IT WAS MADE. IDocumentAccessResolver runs seven gates in a fixed order and every one fails closed: a resolved company, an employee identity, the document's own company, a registered family AND owner resolver, THE RELATION - the owning record's company resolved independently and required to agree, which is what makes the company column mean something - then the owning module's own CanAsync, then confidentiality, which above Internal demands a SECOND CanAsync at the manage tier. IPlatformDocumentService was verified member by member: all eleven resolve the context through one ScopeAsync and call that resolver before they touch or return a row. AND THE PROOF IS NOW A TEST, NOT A READING. Crediting a SERVICE means a future member that forgot to authorize would be credited too, which is the CORRECTION-004 shape exactly. DocumentAuthorityMemberTests enumerates the interface BY REFLECTION and fails when a member is added that it does not drive, then drives every member through a recording resolver and asserts both that it asked and that a refusal stopped it - no row written, no status changed, no blob left behind. DocumentAuthoritySurfaceTests pins the analyzer boundary: the two declared types are credited, an identically-shaped undeclared look-alike is not, IDocumentStorage is not (storing a file is not deciding who may), and a bare POST is still caught. THE CONTROLLER COUNT MOVES FOR A DIFFERENT REASON: RestaurantIntelligenceController, a READ-ONLY screen with one GET and no mutating action at all - so 51 -> 52 controllers with no endpoint of its own in this total. It was integrated with [SessionValidation] and [InvPerm("read")] added; the held version had neither, and would have rendered empty to an anonymous caller, which looks safe and is a data accident rather than an authorization. DEBT UNCHANGED AT 94, and the gap set is identical id for id - no entry added, none removed, no re-bless, no suppression, and the final candidate produced ZERO CBA001/CBA004/CBA006. Attribute-protected does not move: all three new endpoints authorize in body. 157 + 188 + 94 = 439. WHAT THE AUTHORITY DECLARATION DID NOT DO, measured rather than assumed: it reclassified NO existing endpoint. inBodyProtected moved by exactly the three new endpoints and gaps did not move at all, so nothing already in the debt was quietly credited by the new names.

TWO new POST endpoints on a NEW controller, ProjectCloseoutController - Close and Reopen - so the controller count moves 50 -> 51 alongside the endpoint total. Both are protected in body on arrival: each resolves the BusinessContext and asks IProjectsAccessService for 'close' on a ForProject target, with [ValidateAntiForgeryToken]. NO NEW PROJECTS ACTION WAS INVENTED - 'close' already existed in the vocabulary, answered only for the module role and refused on the membership path, which is exactly the authority freezing a project's financial history should need. THE CONTROLLER GATE IS A SECOND CHECK, NOT THE ONLY ONE. ProjectCloseoutService re-evaluates readiness and re-checks authority before it writes, so 'the button was enabled' can never be the reason a project closed. The controller gate exists because an endpoint whose guard is invisible at the endpoint is one nobody can audit by reading it - and the analyzer, correctly, would not credit it either: CBA001 fired on both endpoints until the gate was stated there. NO BASELINE ENTRY WAS ADDED OR REMOVED and the final candidate produced ZERO CBA004. Purely descriptive - mutating 434 -> 436, inBodyProtected 183 -> 185, attributeProtected unchanged at 157 because both authorize in body, and gaps UNCHANGED at 94 with the gap set identical id for id. 157 + 185 + 94 = 436. WHAT IS NOT IN THIS INCREMENT, and deliberately: financial reversal of a posted progress billing. It is blocked on an AR receipt reversal foundation that is still not landed - IReceivableService publishes CreateReceiptAsync and nothing that undoes one - and posting a billing creates real Receipt rows for retention and advance recovery, so the missing capability is load-bearing for the ordinary case rather than an edge one. Closeout therefore treats an un-reversible posted billing as a WARNING rather than a blocker: a blocker nobody can satisfy is a project that never closes. No diagnostic was suppressed, no analyzer rule weakened, no permission loosened and none of the 94 existing gaps was removed.

frozenBaselineHistory.stage: Roster and shift management (TAB-2 implementation / TAB-1 reconciliation, 2026-08-31)
frozenBaselineHistory.note: FOUR new POST endpoints on a NEW controller, RosterController - CreatePeriod, Assign, CancelAssignment and Publish - so the controller count moves 49 -> 50 alongside the endpoint total. All four are protected in body on arrival: each resolves the BusinessContext and asks IHrAccessService for 'attendance-manage' before it acts, with [ValidateAntiForgeryToken] on every one. NO NEW HR ACTION WAS INVENTED - rostering is workforce-time administration, which is what attendance-manage already means, and inventing roster-manage would have created a second vocabulary for one job. NO BASELINE ENTRY WAS ADDED OR REMOVED and the integrated candidate produced ZERO CBA004: endpoints that arrive protected were never in this list. Purely descriptive - mutating 430 -> 434, inBodyProtected 179 -> 183, attributeProtected unchanged at 157 because all four authorize in body, and gaps UNCHANGED at 94 with the gap set identical id for id. 157 + 183 + 94 = 434. THE CONTROLLER DELTA IS +1 FROM 49, NOT FROM 48. The candidate was measured by its author against dd112cc, before DocumentsController landed and moved the count; re-measuring on the current base is what caught it, and copying the author's constants would have frozen a number that was already stale. READ PATHS ARE NOT IN THESE FIGURES. An employee reads their OWN published roster with no attendance authority - the service takes the employee from the resolved BusinessContext rather than a parameter, and queries published assignments only, so a draft schedule is invisible and a colleague's is unreachable. GETs are not mutating endpoints and this file does not track them. A BOOTSTRAP NOTE, RECORDED RATHER THAN CHANGED: attendance-manage is bootstrap-open, so on an install with no HR roles configured roster management is exactly as open as attendance administration already is. That is inherited posture, not new exposure, and reusing the existing action is what kept it from becoming a new decision. Making rostering less open than attendance would need a NeverBootstrapOpen entry plus a new action - a deliberate owner change, not a side effect of this batch. Carried forward as HR ATTENDANCE/ROSTER BOOTSTRAP POLICY REVIEW. No diagnostic was suppressed, no analyzer rule weakened, no permission loosened and none of the 94 existing gaps was removed.

FOUR new POST endpoints on a NEW controller, EmployeeOnboardingController - Start, CompleteItem, WaiveItem and Complete - so the controller count moves 47 -> 48 alongside the endpoint total. All four are protected in body from the moment they land: each resolves the BusinessContext, refuses when no company resolves, and asks IHrAccessService.CanAsync for 'employee-manage' before it acts, with [ValidateAntiForgeryToken] on every one. The service then re-asks the precise per-employee question, so the controller gate is a coarse pre-check rather than the only check. NO BASELINE ENTRY WAS ADDED OR REMOVED and the integrated candidate produced ZERO CBA004 - an endpoint that arrives protected was never in this list, so nothing was stale. Purely descriptive: mutating 426 -> 430, inBodyProtected 175 -> 179, attributeProtected unchanged at 157 because all four authorize in body rather than by attribute, and gaps UNCHANGED at 94 with the gap set identical id for id. 157 + 179 + 94 = 430. SELF-SERVICE IS DELIBERATELY ASYMMETRIC and none of it is in these four numbers: an employee with no HR role may READ their own onboarding, may not read a colleague's, and may not complete, waive or finish anything. Read paths are not mutating endpoints and this file does not track them. Waiver in particular stays an explicit management operation carrying an actor, a reason and a timestamp - it records who excused a requirement and why, and never marks it complete. No diagnostic was suppressed, no analyzer rule weakened, no permission loosened, and none of the 94 existing gaps was removed to make anything green.

frozenBaselineHistory.stage: Project billing separation of duties, batch 1 (TAB-6 implementation / TAB-1 reconciliation, 2026-08-30)
frozenBaselineHistory.note: TWO new POST endpoints on the EXISTING ProjectController - SubmitBilling and ReturnBilling - so the controller count does not move. Both are protected in body from the moment they land, through IProjectsAccessService.CanAsync on a PermissionTarget.ForProject before they act, with the actor taken from the resolved BusinessContext and every refusal answering identically so the endpoint cannot be used to probe which projects exist. NO BASELINE ENTRY WAS ADDED OR REMOVED, and the integrated candidate produced ZERO CBA004: an endpoint that arrives protected was never in this list, so there was nothing stale to resolve. This increment is therefore purely descriptive - mutating 424 -> 426 and inBodyProtected 173 -> 175, attributeProtected unchanged at 157 because both authorize in body rather than by attribute, and gaps UNCHANGED at 94 with the gap set identical id for id. 157 + 175 + 94 = 426. WHAT THE ENDPOINTS ARE FOR, because the authorization shape is the point of the batch. The single 'billing' right covered preparing, approving and posting, which makes separation of duties impossible to express: holding it once is holding it for the whole lifecycle. It is split into billing-prepare, billing-approve and billing-post. The old 'billing' action is KEPT and unchanged - advance receipt, retention release and subcontractor billing still use it. billing-post carries the same accounting requirement the old single right did: it demands Accounting 'post', which is on the NeverBootstrapOpen list, so no Projects-side bootstrap can imply a ledger effect. Preparing and approving deliberately do NOT demand it, because neither touches the ledger and requiring the posting right to approve would have made the split worthless. Whether a given approver may approve a given billing is a RECORD-level question a module access service cannot answer - it is not given the document - so ProgressBillingService refuses when CreatedBy equals the actor, and refuses a billing with no recorded preparer rather than waving it through, since an unknown preparer cannot be shown to be someone other than this approver. No diagnostic was suppressed, no analyzer rule weakened, no permission loosened and no unrelated debt re-blessed to reach these numbers.

frozenBaselineHistory.stage: HR authorization foundation (TAB-2 implementation / TAB-1 reconciliation, 2026-08-30)
frozenBaselineHistory.note: FORTY-TWO baseline entries REMOVED, which is the only direction this list may move. Every one of them was a live HR mutation carrying no authorization at all - holiday, attendance, final settlement, HR document and contract, leave accrual and policy, salary and attendance policy, employee, appraisal, training, recruitment, job title, leave API and employee self-service actions across AdminController, its Appraisals/Recruitment/Training partials, HrApiController, LeaveApiController and PeopleController. Each now authorizes in body through IHrAccessService.CanAsync before it acts, so CBA004 FIRED on all forty-two and was resolved by removing their entries. The analyzer's own message is the evidence: 'it is now authorized in-body via IHrAccessService.CanAsync'. So gaps 136 -> 94 and inBodyProtected 131 -> 173, while mutating stays 424 and attributeProtected stays 157 - no endpoint was added or removed, and none of the forty-two is protected by an attribute. The arithmetic still closes: 157 + 173 + 94 = 424. TWO SECURITY DETAILS WORTH RECORDING. SaveMainPolices takes leave-manage AND ADDITIONALLY payroll-manage when the payload actually carries SalaryPolicies, because that one endpoint can move base salary, allowances, overtime, penalties, social insurance and tax rate; a single weaker HR permission would have closed the gap while opening payroll. And the four self-service mutations - CreateLeave, CreateRequest, AcknowledgeAppraisal and LeaveApiController.Create - use the employee-request capability added in 3d1355b, which is self-only above both the bootstrap branch and the role rules, so closing them did not hand a self-service POST authority over anyone else's record. THE 94 THAT REMAIN ARE NOT HR DEBT. Three HR-registry endpoints are deliberately excluded - AddHierarchicalItem, AdministrativeBodiesCompany and JobTitle - because they administer companies, branches, job titles and the shared administrative hierarchy rather than HR, and belong to a different owner; they stay in this list. The other 91 are pre-existing debt in other modules, untouched here. NO entry was added, no entry was edited, no CBA diagnostic was suppressed, no analyzer rule was weakened and no permission was loosened to reach these numbers.

frozenBaselineHistory.stage: Quotation business conversation convergence (TAB-3 endpoint / TAB-1 reconciliation, 2026-08-29)
frozenBaselineHistory.note: ONE new POST endpoint on the EXISTING InventoryController - QuotationConversationAdd - so the controller count does not move. It is protected in body from the moment it lands: it resolves the company server-side, requires a BusinessContext with a real employee, and asks InventoryAccessService for the 'doc' action on PermissionTarget.ForEntity(EntityRegistry.Quotation, id) before it writes. Adding to a record's discussion is a mutation of that record's history, so it claims the module's document ability rather than 'read'; a caller who may not change the quotation may not add to its conversation. It refuses with NotFound semantics identical to the read path's, so neither endpoint is an existence oracle for a quotation in another company. The companion GET, QuotationConversation, is not mutating and this file does not track it. So mutating moves 423 -> 424 and inBodyProtected 130 -> 131, attributeProtected is unchanged at 157, and the arithmetic still closes: 157 + 131 + 136 = 424. GAPS DO NOT MOVE AND MUST NOT: 136 before, 136 after, the gap set identical id for id. NO entry was added, removed or edited, CBA001 does not fire on the new endpoint, no diagnostic was suppressed, no Inventory permission was weakened and the endpoint was not marked ignored or reclassified. This is a descriptive reconciliation of one more mutating endpoint that arrived already protected - not a re-bless, which would mean accepting unprotected code by moving the debt figure.

Seven ProjectController mutating actions that carried NO authorization at all - SaveProject, DeleteProject, SaveProgress, ConfirmProgress, DeleteProgress, SaveActivityType and DeleteActivityType - now authorize in-body through IProjectsAccessService.CanAsync before they act, so CBA004 REQUIRED their baseline entries to be removed. That is a shrink of 7: gaps 143 -> 136 and the entries list 143 -> 136. The same pass added the project membership writer (dbo.ProjectMembers previously had two readers and no writer), whose three mutating actions - AddMember, UpdateMember and EndMember - are in-body protected from the moment they land, so mutating moves 420 -> 423 and inBodyProtected 120 -> 130 (+7 closed, +3 new). The arithmetic still closes: 157 + 130 + 136 = 423. NO entry was added, no entry was edited, no CBA diagnostic was suppressed, and the shrink-only rule was not relaxed - the debt list only got shorter. The pass also removed all 61 uses of the hardcoded DefaultCompanyId = 1 and gated all 16 pre-existing GET screens, neither of which this file tracks because GETs are not mutating endpoints.

Report Studio V1 added ONE controller, ReportStudioApiController, with FIVE endpoints - Fields, Validate, Preview, Save and Export. Growth is +5 mutating and +5 in-body protected, +0 attribute-protected and +0 debt, and the arithmetic still closes: 157 + 115 + 143 = 415. Every one of the five authorizes in-body through IReportAuthorizationService.AuthorizeReportAsync at the boundary before it acts, resolving the dataset's report definition from the caller's own permitted list. CBA001 FIRED ON ALL FOUR POSTS when the controller first landed and was fixed by ADDING THAT GATE - not by a baseline entry, not by a suppression, and not by reshaping a write as a GET. NO entry was added, removed or edited; the gap figure stays 143 and the entries list is byte-identical; no CBA diagnostic was suppressed and the shrink-only rule was not relaxed. Only the descriptive totals moved, because production code was added - the case this file's own rules paragraph describes.
The accepted Stage 1 measurement. Reproduced exactly by the Roslyn analyzer with 0 classification disagreements across all 388 endpoints.

Batch A added three mutating endpoints - PlatformGrantsApiController.Create, .Revoke and .UpdateValidity - and one controller. All three are authorized in-body through IPlatformGrantWriter, which resolves the actor's administration tier and privilege ceiling via the real module access services. DEBT IS UNCHANGED AT 143 and no entry was added, removed or edited: the gap set still matches this file id for id. Only the descriptive totals moved, because production code was added.

Reconciles the descriptive totals with the modernization work that had accumulated in the working tree unrecorded. Growth is +19 mutating and +19 in-body protected, +0 attribute-protected and +0 debt - the signature of protected endpoints being added, and the arithmetic still closes: 157 + 110 + 143 = 410. COMPOSITION OF THE +19, every one authorized in-body through a real access service on the analyzer's approved authority list: (a) SEVEN Reporting write endpoints on ReportsCenterWriteApiController - SaveLayout, Fork, SetDefault, DeleteLayout, AddFavorite, RemoveFavorite, ReorderFavorites - each through IReportAuthorizationService.AuthorizeReportAsync or .AuthorizeTemplateAsync; (b) ELEVEN Tasks endpoints on TasksController - the Task Ecosystem checklist (Add/Remove/Reorder/Toggle), dependencies (Add/Remove), templates (Apply/Save/SetActive), BoardMove and TaskCommentAdd - each through ITasksAccessService.CanAsync; (c) ONE Calendar endpoint, CalendarController.SaveSchedule, through ICalendarAccessService.CanEventAsync. VERIFIED INDEPENDENTLY, not merely asserted: the gap set was rebuilt from the analyzer's own evidence file (docs/architecture/evidence/Roslyn-Authorization-Inventory.csv, written by the same run) and differenced against this file's entries - 143 vs 143, with ZERO ids present in the analyzer and absent here (which would be new debt) and ZERO present here and absent in the analyzer (which would be a stale entry). CalendarController.Save and .Delete are unauthorized but are NOT new debt: both were already frozen entries in this file, so Calendar arrived carrying pre-existing debt rather than adding to it. NO entry was added, removed or edited; the gap figure stays 143; no CBA diagnostic was suppressed and no baseline shrink-only rule was relaxed.

frozenBaselineHistory.stage: UAT dataset harness controller-count reconciliation (UAT dataset owner, 2026-08-12)
frozenBaselineHistory.note: Controller-count-only reconciliation for UatSeedController, the [DevOnly] UAT dataset harness on api/uat introduced by the UAT dataset owner. The analyzer's frozen CONTROLLER count moves 44 -> 45; NONE of the four figures that matter moves. Mutating stays 410, attribute-protected 157, in-body-protected 110 and debt 143, and 157 + 110 + 143 = 410 still closes. THE REASON IS MECHANICAL, not a judgement: every action on that controller is [HttpGet] - preflight, prime, seed, counts, cleanup - so the analyzer models the controller but finds no mutating endpoint on it to classify. VERIFIED INDEPENDENTLY rather than asserted: the analyzer's own evidence file docs/architecture/evidence/Roslyn-Authorization-Inventory.csv holds 410 rows and ZERO of them name UatSeed, which is the same 410 the frozen mutating total asserts, so the new controller contributed nothing to any protected category and nothing to the debt. NO entry in this file was added, removed or edited; count stays 143 and entries stays 143. No CBA diagnostic was suppressed, CBA001 was not weakened, no security attribute was removed, and no product authorization was changed to satisfy a count. The controller is not an unmeasured hole: it returns 404 outside Development via [CrossBuy.Models.DevOnly], is shared-key gated, and its own preflight refuses to write unless the live connection resolves to CrossBuyDev. Also recorded here: the passwordless GET api/uat/signin that briefly existed on this controller has been REMOVED in the same increment; UAT runtime automation now authenticates through the ordinary AccountController.Login / PasswordSignInAsync path.
